portion_doctrine: Lightroom tutorials = repetitive instructional video transcripts with embedded tactical doctrine on masking, color grading, batch editing, and HDR merging. Real content density: 40-50% actionable. Primary value: specific slider behaviors, mask combination patterns, and recommended feathering/flow workflows.
operating_rules: Feathering must be dialed per-use, not left at 100% default, for natural mask transitions
Auto-align and auto-settings recommended as first step in HDR merge dialog
Radial gradient invert toggle essential for center-spotlight vs surround-vignette effects
Alt/Option-click on parameter label (e.g., 'Highlights') resets that slider group only
Double-click slider value or word to reset individual control
Select subject + luminance range subtraction creates highlight-specific masks
Mixer with click-on-image hue/sat/luminance tool preferred over slider-only workflow
De-ghosting set to medium for HDR with movement (trees, people in wind)
Subtle presets recommended (avoid strong before applying, adjust amount slider after) for shareability
White balance not always perfect-neutral: creative warmth/coolness acceptable if skin looks natural

steps: Select 2+ raw files at different exposures
Right-click > photo merge > HDR
Check auto-align and auto-settings
Adjust de-ghosting to medium if movement present
Click merge
Edit image to desired state
Presets > plus icon > create preset
Name preset and choose group (user presets)
Uncheck all > check only modified parameters
Create > right-click preset > show in finder > .xmp file can be zipped and sold online

named_methods.method: Batch edit multiple images with sync
steps: Edit reference image (make it primary with brightest thumbnail)
Library module > select reference + shift-click others
Sync settings button > check all or selective only
Synchronize (replaces or merges masks per dialog)

named_methods.method: Advanced mask: subject with highlight-only effect
steps: Create mask: select subject
Add adjustment (e.g., bring up highlights)
Create new mask: select subject again
Subtract luminance range (choose shadows)
Only highlights now affected on subject
Crop tool > angle icon
Draw line along horizon feature
Auto applies horizontal correction
Create radial gradient mask behind subject (expose + warm)
Subtract subject from mask (removes overlap)
Create separate highlight-only mask on subject with highlight glow
Result: light behind + light on face without doubling

Select Subject (AI person/object detection)
Select Sky (AI sky isolation)
Select Background (inverse of subject)
Select Objects (paint-to-identify specific items)
Brush mask tool with flow/feathering controls and alt-option subtract mode
Linear gradient (top-to-bottom effect masking)
Radial gradient (center-out effect masking, invertible)
Color range (select by hue with tolerance slider)
Luminance range (select by brightness with range slider)
Mixer (HSL per-color adjustments with visual click-on-image tool)
Point color (sample-specific hue/sat/luminance fine-tuning)
Calibration (edit RGB primaries globally, subtle)
Photo Merge > HDR (auto-align, auto-settings, de-ghosting, stacking)
Transform tab (vertical/horizontal perspective, auto-vertical for architecture)
Adaptive presets (AI-driven: sky, subject, background blur, portrait retouching)
AI style advisor (learns from past edits, suggests presets)
Batch editor (blanket adjustments across multiple images)
Profiles (Adobe color, monochrome, portrait, artistic templates)
Straighten tool (angle via line trace or slider)
Crop presets (1:1, 5x7, 16:9, unlock for custom)
Generative expand (Photoshop integration: AI canvas extension)
Film simulation (RAWTherapee: match colors from reference photo without cube files)
prompts_and_commands: Hold alt/option + click 'Tone' label to reset all tone controls at once
Press R to open crop tool
Double-click word (e.g., 'Highlights') to reset that slider only
Click + hold eyeball next to parameter to toggle before/after
Shift-click to select multiple images for batch
Right-click > show in finder to locate preset .xmp file
Mask > show overlay to visualize affected area with red tint
Mask > invert (radio/linear gradient icon) to flip center/surround logic
Mask > luminance range slider to expand/contract color isolation
Feathering slider reduces hard edge transition on brush/gradient masks
numbers_and_specifics: HDR: up to 9 exposures can be merged in one photo merge
De-ghosting: recommend medium setting for movement-heavy scenes
Preset lifetime cost: Luminar Neo $50/year vs Lightroom $10+/month (~$120/year)
Feathering: 100% default, manually reduce per-mask for soft edges
Flow: reduce below 100% for gradual brush build-up instead of one-pass saturation
Color picker: click on image with mixer tool to target hue/sat/luminance by color region
content_ideas: Advanced mask subtraction for light painting behind subjects
Feathering as the unlock for invisible mask edges
Preset creation as affiliate revenue (sell packs of 10 .xmp files)
HDR for landscape and architecture detail recovery
Batch editing workflow for event photography (uniform lighting correction across series)
Color grading via point color for archive-specific color palette (autumn foliage boost, sky cyan)
Mixer click-on-image preferred over sliders for intuitive color editing
Lightroom as file organization and renaming tool independent of editing
gates_and_constraints: Cube file presets not importable into some older DAMs (RAWTherapee offers film simulation workaround)
AI-driven masks (subject, sky) can fail on complex backgrounds or edge cases (requires manual brush refinement)
Preset amount slider UI hidden until preset applied (not visible in create dialog)
De-ghosting cannot fully eliminate moving subjects (trees in wind, people shifting) - residual ghosts visible at high blur amounts
Perspective transform (full auto) stretches people unnaturally - best for architecture only
contradictions: Feathering best practice: dial per-mask vs. workflow reality suggests batch feathering 60-80% as default faster approach
White balance: precision (gray card method, neutral target) vs. creative (intentional warmth) positioning not reconciled
Vibrance over saturation for people, but point color saturation still used in advanced session (dual tool necessity)
Presets recommended 'subtle' but real-world results often weak - users then increase amount slider, contradicting subtlety goal
Mask blending slider (0 = isolated, 100 = blended) vs. feathering slider (0 = hard, 100 = soft) dual-control redundancy not explained
weird_gold: Gray card white balance workflow mentioned but discounted: 'as shot usually fine' - gray card precision not valued in tutorial
De-ghosting UI: 'amount' slider labeled for 'medium' but no values given, relies on user eyeball judgment
Preset export: .xmp files are XML text - users can open, edit, and redistribute (no encryption, pure trust model)
Feathering per-mask creates infinite variation: same adjustment, different feathering = visual difference from subtle to obvious
HDR stacking preserves originals in stack folder - non-destructive, but mental model can confuse which is final for export
Luminance range subtract: red overlay shows future adjustment area in real-time, crucial UX feature not highlighted as powerful
skills_identified: Mask subtraction (combining select + subtract for complex effects)
boilerplate_estimate: 35-40% of segments 21-25 is UI navigation, opening/closing sequences, sponsor segments, and repeated 'thanks for watching' scaffolding. Real technique content: 60-65%.
